hypothesis: At 9a4caa7b, the Muon optimizer in train.py performs the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization for every 2-D weight matrix redundantly on all 4 ranks (train.py exposes --compile-muon/--nki-muon/--muon-lr-fp32 but no ownership option, whereas the sibling research/scratch/fresh_start_train.py at the same commit has --experimental-optimizer-ownership, which the fs-w65 ledger row records as an exact-numerics, +5.06% complete-step gain and which every later fresh-start KEEP stack retained). Partitioning the Newton-Schulz work across ranks (each rank orthogonalizes only the parameters it owns, in zero-padded static-shape batches, then the results are all-gathered so every rank applies identical updates) is mathematically neutral and removes 3/4 of the per-step orthogonalization compute from the critical path. In the fixed 1800 s budget this converts to more optimizer steps at unchanged per-step loss, lowering public_val_bpb. The bf16-sdpa-input KEEP (2233 vs 2076 steps -> 1.002028 vs 1.005967) shows that a pure step-rate gain of this order converts to roughly -0.0005 BPB per +1% steps in this regime. This lane (optimizer work partition) is orthogonal to the pending norm-output/SDPA precision boundaries, so it remains additive if those KEEP.
implementation_plan: All edits confined to train.py on branch autoloop/20260922-muon-owner-compute-ns-default-shape from 9a4caa7b; reference code may be read (not copied verbatim if names differ) from research/scratch/fresh_start_train.py at the same commit under its --experimental-optimizer-ownership path. STEP 1 (static inspection, recorded only as a note in the implementation summary; no artifact file required): locate the Muon optimizer class in train.py -- the optimizer whose step() applies momentum/Nesterov to gradients of 2-D weight matrices and then calls the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization routine (the function referenced by --compile-muon / --nki-muon selection). Determine whether every rank executes the orthogonalization for every Muon parameter (redundant) or whether work is already split by rank followed by a collective. If already split, stop and report HALT-INERT. STEP 2 (toggle): following the --bf16-sdpa-input pattern, add module-level USE_MUON_OWNER_COMPUTE = True with env override NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_MUON_OWNER_COMPUTE ('0' disables), argparse pair --muon-owner-compute / --no-muon-owner-compute (dest muon_owner_compute, default None -> constant), resolved in main() before the optimizer is constructed; default must resolve True so the candidate run uses no flags. Do not add it to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES (it does not affect the forward pass, checkpointed weights, or evaluation). STEP 3 (partition): in Muon.step, keep the existing momentum-buffer update, Nesterov blend, LR/weight-decay application and parameter iteration order exactly as they are for all ranks. Only wrap the orthogonalization: for each existing same-shape batch (or, if the current code orthogonalizes per-parameter, treat each parameter list of identical shape as a batch), when USE_MUON_OWNER_COMPUTE and torch.distributed is initialized with world_size > 1: (a) n = number of matrices in the batch, per_rank = ceil(n / world_size); (b) rank r owns indices r*per_rank ... min((r+1)*per_rank, n)-1 (contiguous deterministic ownership; identical on all ranks because parameter order is deterministic); (c) build a zero-padded local input stack of static shape [per_rank, *matrix_shape] containing the owned momentum-updated gradients (zeros in padding slots); (d) call the SAME orthogonalization routine the existing code would have called (plain, compiled, or NKI, whichever the existing flags select -- do not change that selection) on the local stack; a zero matrix must yield a zero result, so keep the existing normalization epsilon guard and do not divide by an unguarded norm; (e) all_gather the local result stacks with torch.distributed.all_gather_into_tensor into a [world_size*per_rank, *matrix_shape] tensor (fall back to torch.distributed.all_gather on a list if all_gather_into_tensor is unavailable on the active backend), using the default process group; (f) slice the first n entries in ownership order and use them exactly where the original code used the full orthogonalized batch; padding entries are discarded. If the existing code applies a shape-dependent scale factor (e.g. sqrt(max(1, rows/cols))) after orthogonalization, apply it unchanged to the gathered results. When the toggle is False or world_size == 1, execute the original code path unchanged. Do not modify the momentum state layout (all ranks keep full buffers so optimizer state and checkpoint format are unchanged), gradient all-reduce, clipping, --clip-after-reduce/--grad-bucket logic, Adam/ngram-ve optimizers, schedules, model, data, or evaluation code. STEP 4 (logging): add exactly one field 'muon_owner_compute=<bool>' to the existing sched_tricks/optimizer config oneliner printed at startup. STEP 5 (self-review in the implementation summary, static only): state the diff is limited to the toggle/env/CLI resolution, the Muon.step ownership block, and the one log field; state that with NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_MUON_OWNER_COMPUTE=0 or world_size==1 the original branch executes; state that forward/eval code, ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES, checkpoint format and optimizer state tensors are unchanged. No CPU execution, unit test, compilation output, dtype log or hardware result is required before the implementation gate; runtime verification is the Operator's smoke run (muon_owner_compute=True in the oneliner, num_params_M 592.9, all other oneliners identical to control, causality_passed True, >= 338 steps, step-rate ratio >= 1.01 vs same-host control smoke, public_val_bpb within +/-0.002 of same-host control smoke). Launch the full run with the exact control launch command and environment (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2 torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=4 train.py --num-steps 5000 --max-train-seconds 1800 --seed 42; NEURON_CC_FLAGS='--optlevel=1', NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_SEED=42, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1) and no additional flags.
single_causal_change: One optimizer-implementation change confined to train.py: inside Muon.step, when USE_MUON_OWNER_COMPUTE is True and dist world_size > 1, the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization of the momentum-updated gradients is computed only for rank-owned parameters (deterministic round-robin ownership over each existing same-shape batch, zero-padded so every rank executes an identical static shape), and the orthogonalized results are exchanged with one torch.distributed all_gather so that every rank then applies exactly the same update to every parameter. Momentum/Nesterov buffer maintenance, LR/weight-decay application, parameter order, the selected Newton-Schulz backend (plain / compiled / NKI, whichever the existing flags select), gradient all-reduce, clipping, model, data, seed, budget, evaluator and launch shape are untouched. When the toggle is off or world_size == 1 the original code path executes unchanged. Comparison: same-host pinned control on public_val_bpb (trn21 2071 / 1.005734; trn22 2076 / 1.005967). Outcome classes in order: (1) HALT-INERT if static inspection finds Muon already partitions Newton-Schulz across ranks (then no patch, no run); (2) HALT-NUMERICS if smoke steps are >= control smoke but smoke public_val_bpb differs from the same-host control smoke (1.165855 trn21 / 1.165604 trn22) by more than 0.002 in either direction (partition changed the math, not just the speed; no full run); (3) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if full-run steps < 90% of same-host control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22); (4) FALSIFIED-INERT if full-run steps within +/-1% of control (redundant Newton-Schulz is not a measurable cost at this model size); (5) EXCESS-GAIN-REVIEW if steps > +10% of control (>2278 trn21, >2283 trn22): compare logged validation trajectories at matched step counts before any quality claim; SUCCESS only if public_val_bpb < control by >= 0.001 and no matched-step deficit > 0.010 at the control's final step; (6) SUCCESS if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb < same-host control by >= 0.001; (7) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb >= control; (8) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise (including +2% steps with a BPB gain smaller than 0.001).
